GPU.Description: Integrated GPU block of the Apple M4 SoC (28 billion transistors total). Apple ships a 10-core GPU in Mac mini, iMac, MacBook Pro and most iPad Pro configurations; the entry-level 256 GB/512 GB 11-inch iPad Pro uses a binned 9-core part. The GPU reports Metal GPU family Apple9 and adds Dynamic Caching (on-chip memory allocated to registers, threadgroup memory and stack in hardware at run time), hardware-accelerated ray tracing and hardware-accelerated mesh shading. It shares unified memory with the CPU and Neural Engine at 120 GB/s

GPU Core.Description: Apple GPU core: 128 FP32 ALUs organized as 4 SIMD pipelines of 32 lanes, giving 1280 ALUs across the 10-core GPU. The 32-thread SIMD-group width is documented by Apple (Metal Feature Set Tables, Apple9); the 128-ALU-per-core figure follows Apple's published M-series GPU ratios and is corroborated by independent microarchitecture analysis. Apple does not publish per-core register file, L1 or L2 cache capacities for the M3/M4 generation, and Dynamic Caching makes the register/threadgroup split dynamic rather than fixed. Each core also provides the hardware ray-tracing and mesh-shading blocks; Apple does not publish their per-core counts

SIMD Pipeline.Description: 32-wide SIMD execution pipeline. Each pipeline issues one instruction per cycle for one 32-thread SIMD-group, and 4 pipelines per core account for the core's 128 ALUs. The SIMD-group width of 32 and the 1024-thread maximum threadgroup size are Apple-documented Metal limits; the 4-pipeline decomposition is inferred from the ALU count and community microarchitecture analysis, as Apple does not document the dispatch structure

Threadgroup Memory.description: Maximum threadgroup (shared) memory allocation per threadgroup is 32 KB for the Apple9 GPU family (Apple Metal Feature Set Tables); maximum threads per threadgroup is 1024 and maximum buffer length is 2 GB. On M3-generation and later GPUs this storage is drawn from the Dynamic Caching on-chip pool that also backs registers and stack, so the physical pool size per core is not a published constant

Unified Memory.description: LPDDR5X unified memory shared by CPU, GPU, Neural Engine and media engine with zero-copy access. Apple publishes 120 GB/s of memory bandwidth and configurations of 16 GB, 24 GB or 32 GB; the 32 GB maximum is recorded here. The 128-bit bus width is the arithmetic match for 120 GB/s at LPDDR5X-7500 (Apple does not state bus width directly). LPDDR5X is reported as LPDDR5 above because the schema enum has no LPDDR5X value. Apple publishes no GPU L1/L2 or system-level cache sizes for M4, so no cache levels are listed

LLVMFeatures.Name: air64
LLVMFeatures.Description: Apple Intermediate Representation (AIR), the LLVM-bitcode-based IR emitted by Apple's metal compiler (-target air64-apple-macos<version>, or air64-apple-ios<version> for iPadOS). AIR is Apple-private and is not an upstream LLVM backend target; there is no public LLVM target for the Apple GPU ISA

PowerStates.Name: Active
PowerStates.Description: GPU active. Apple publishes neither GPU clock frequencies nor a chip- or GPU-level TDP for M4, so BaseClock, BoostClock and MaxTDP are omitted rather than estimated; third-party measurements of the M4 GPU peak clock disagree (1.68-1.80 GHz)

PowerStates.Name: Idle
PowerStates.Description: Low-power state when no GPU work is scheduled; frequency and voltage are managed by the SoC power controller
